Weekly Briefing12 July 20266 min read

Where formal institutions fall short

A short summary of the piece.

narrative.overview:
Every section of the site is issued like a paper in one series: a coloured series band carrying the series line and a number, a Caslon title, an author line, keywords, a ruled abstract box, and a numbered contents list. The look borrows from two plain sources at once: the cover sheet of an economics working paper and the unstyled academic homepage, with blue underlined links. The site's credibility comes from how plain it is. Nothing is shown off. Everything is filed.

The paper is white, the ink is warm near-black, and structure comes from warm grey hairlines rather than from boxes, fills or shadows. Colour is spent in one place per section, the 6px band above the title, plus that section's figures and its active navigation. The site and the writing take oxblood. Each research tool has its own accent, all tuned to a similar mid-dark weight so none of them shouts. Density is that of a reading page: generous line height and a 42rem prose measure. Inside the tools, data rows run dense with tabular figures.

Reading surfaces (About, guide, writing, Ask) use the reading face throughout. Operating surfaces (the six tools, OneBook, Tradewinds) keep the same cover sheet and chrome, but their controls stay standard and use the system sans.
keyCharacteristics: A 6px series band in the section's colour opens every section, with the series line ("Working Paper Series, No. NN") and a date or scope on a hairline-ruled strip.
Libre Caslon Text for titles and prose, the system sans for navigation, labels and tool UI, IBM Plex Mono only for code and figures.
Indexes are numbered, hairline-ruled rows. Never cards.
Flat: no shadows, square or near-square corners, hairline borders.
Blue underlined links, offset 0.18em, as on an academic homepage.

rules.name: The One Band Rule
rules.body: A section owns exactly one colour. It appears on the 6px band, the contents numbers, the active nav and the lead data series. It never appears as a fill behind text or as a page background.

rules.name: The Ink Marks Place Rule
rules.body: The site bar shows the current section with an ink underline (2px, offset 0.4em), never a colour. Section navs use their own band colour for the underline.

rules.name: The Severity Is Not Accent Rule
rules.body: Severity and P&L colours (seismic red, gain, loss, critical) are reserved for encoding data. OneBook's gain and loss are never used as categorical colours.

rules.name: The Weight 400 Rule
rules.body: h1 to h3 are Caslon at 400. Emphasis comes from size and placement. The only semibold on the site is the sans label heading.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase, no tracked-out labels, no kickers. Section labels are plain sentence-case sans at label size.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Tables and every tool section set `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`, so figures line up.

rules.name: The Ruled Not Raised Rule
rules.body: Never lift a surface with a shadow. If something needs separation, give it a hairline. If it needs emphasis, give it an ink rule (the abstract box) or the section's band.

dos: open every new section or tool with the cover sheet: a 6px band in the section's colour, "Working Paper Series, No. NN", title, byline, keywords, and a ruled abstract.
list any index as numbered hairline rows (2.5rem number column, 16px row padding, right meta column).
set titles and prose in Libre Caslon Text at 400, and UI, labels and controls in the system sans.
give a new tool one accent at the same mid-dark weight as the others, with border, hover-border and dim variants derived from it at about 16%, 42% and 8% alpha, sitting on the shared tool paper.
make inline links blue and underlined. Mark the current place with a 2px underline.
keep tool figures tabular, and respect `prefers-reduced-motion` in every tool scope.
donts: use cards, shadows or rounded panels for indexes or content blocks.
use uppercase labels, tracked-out kickers or eyebrows above titles.
spend a section's colour on fills or backgrounds. It belongs to the band, the numbers, the active nav and the lead series.
use bold for headings. Caslon stays at 400.
use severity, gain or loss colours for categories.
hard-code hex values in components when a section token exists.
